proposal.title: Private Azure Blob Storage with existing service identity
proposal.body: Scope: one Azure Blob Storage account and container for synthetic documents, using the private-object-storage contract. Public/anonymous blob access is blocked, blob versioning is enabled and encryption uses Microsoft-managed keys. The existing service identity (outside provisioning scope) gets scoped object upload, read and delete access through storage-object-admin. Assumptions: australiaeast is a candidate region, not a verified one. The existing resource group and principal identifiers will be supplied later as required inputs. No compute, AI or private endpoint is included. This is a design only and does not deploy anything.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Anonymous or too-broad access could expose documents. A tightly scoped role limits the damage if credentials leak.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "An existing service identity must upload, read and delete objects. Block anonymous access"
requirementDrafts.statement: Only the existing service identity can upload, read and delete objects in the container. All anonymous access is denied.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Versioning protects against accidental deletes, which matters because the caller has delete rights. Retention of old versions affects storage cost.
requirementDrafts.statement: Blob versioning is enabled so objects can be recovered after an overwrite or delete. Data is encrypted at rest with provider-managed keys.

requirementDrafts.rationale: The country decides which regions are allowed and whether redundancy may copy data across borders.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Use australiaeast as a candidate region"
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: data residency country to be confirmed. australiaeast is only a candidate region.

response.message: Good news: the local Azurite run for revision 2 passed with no failures. That means the generated storage code can upload, read and delete objects against a local stand-in, but it doesn't prove real Entra permissions, versioning, region availability or a real Terraform plan, so there's nothing on the diagram to fix right now. The biggest open item is where the data lives, because that decides whether australiaeast is the right region: should these synthetic documents stay in Australia, or can they be stored in another country?
